questions.question: The rank of $\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\2&4&6\\3&6&9\end{bmatrix}$ is ______.
questions.solution: $R_2-2R_1$ and $R_3-3R_1$ give two zero rows. Only one non-zero row remains, so rank = 1.

questions.title: Rank of idempotent
questions.question: A $3\times3$ real matrix $A$ satisfies $A^2=A$ and $\operatorname{trace}(A)=2$. The rank of $A$ is ______.
questions.solution: Eigenvalues of an idempotent matrix are 0 or 1, and it is diagonalizable. So rank = number of eigenvalues equal to 1 = trace = 2.

questions.title: Maximum rank of nilpotent
questions.question: A real $4\times4$ matrix $A\ne0$ satisfies $A^2=0$. The maximum possible rank of $A$ is
questions.solution: $A^2=0$ means column space $\subseteq$ null space, so $r\le 4-r\Rightarrow r\le2$. Rank 2 is attainable, e.g. $\begin{bmatrix}0&I_2\\0&0\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.title: True statements

questions.solution: (A) true. (B) false since $AB\ne BA$ in general. (C) true. (D) false, determinant is not additive.

questions.solution: Add all columns into the first: every entry becomes $a+b+c=0$, so a zero column appears and $\det=0$.

questions.title: Determinant statements
questions.question: Which statements are TRUE for $n\times n$ real matrices?
questions.solution: $\det(AB)=\det A\det B=\det(BA)$ and $\det A^T=\det A$. The other two are false: $\det(kA)=k^n\det A$, and $\det$ is not additive.

questions.title: Parametric system
questions.question: Consider $x+y+z=6,\; x+2y+3z=10,\; x+2y+\lambda z=\mu$. The system has infinitely many solutions for
questions.solution: $R_3-R_2$ gives $(\lambda-3)z=\mu-10$. If $\lambda=3$ and $\mu=10$, it becomes $0=0$ (rank 2 < 3), so infinite solutions. If $\lambda=3,\mu\ne10$: no solution. If $\lambda\ne3$: unique solution.

questions.solution: Column space must be all of $\mathbb R^m$, so $\operatorname{rank}A=m$ (full row rank).

questions.title: Dimension of span
questions.question: The dimension of the span of $(1,2,3),\ (2,4,6),\ (1,0,1)$ is ______.
questions.solution: $(2,4,6)=2(1,2,3)$, so only $(1,2,3)$ and $(1,0,1)$ are independent. Dimension = 2.

questions.title: Homogeneous square system
questions.question: $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix. Which statements about $Ax=0$ are TRUE?
options: It has a non-trivial solution iff $\det A=0$
Its solution set is a subspace of $\mathbb R^n$
Its solution is unique iff $A$ is singular
questions.solution: (A),(B),(C) are standard. (D) is false: uniqueness (only the zero solution) happens iff $A$ is non-singular.

questions.title: Impossible count
questions.question: Which number of solutions is IMPOSSIBLE for a system of linear equations over $\mathbb R$?
questions.solution: If two distinct solutions $x_1,x_2$ exist, every point $x_1+t(x_2-x_1)$ is also a solution, giving infinitely many.

questions.title: Sum of squares of eigenvalues
questions.question: For $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1&0\\1&2&0\\0&0&3\end{bmatrix}$, the sum of squares of the eigenvalues is ______.
questions.solution: Eigenvalues: $1,3$ (from the top block) and $3$. Sum of squares $=1+9+9=19$. Equivalently $\operatorname{tr}(A^2)=5+5+9=19$.

questions.title: Non-diagonalizable

questions.solution: Only eigenvalue 1 with AM = 2, but $(A-I)v=0$ gives just one independent eigenvector (GM = 1). Not diagonalizable.

questions.title: Cayley-Hamilton value
questions.question: A $2\times2$ matrix $A$ has eigenvalues 2 and 3. The value of $\det(A^2-5A+6I)$ is ______.
questions.solution: The characteristic polynomial is $\lambda^2-5\lambda+6$. By Cayley–Hamilton $A^2-5A+6I=0$, so its determinant is 0.

questions.solution: $A(1,1)^T=(3,3)^T=3(1,1)^T$. For the other eigenvalue $-1$, the eigenvector is $(1,-1)$.
